#1840. Mowbray steps back as Blackburn head coach due to health issues

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Tony Mowbray has stepped back as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to "health issues".

Mowbray returned as Blackburn head coach back in June, having previously spent five years at the club between 2017 and 2022.

Last season, Blackburn struggled for form and were dragged into the relegation battle, eventually finishing 20th to stay in the Championship.

Under Mowbray, they sit 13th in the second tier after 15 games, with 21 points to their name so far (W6 D3 L6).

The 62-year-old had previously resigned as Birmingham City head coach in May 2024, citing health reasons for the decision, and it was later confirmed he had been diagnosed with bowel cancer.

In a statement, Mowbray said: "Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers.

"I'm immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I've loved working with them.

"Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you've given me. It's been a pleasure working alongside you.

Blackburn Rovers wish to share the following statement on behalf of Tony Mowbray. https://t.co/RZDRLanZEq #Rovers https://t.co/L8WaIaebKX

— Blackburn Rovers (@Rovers) November 17, 2026

"To the fans, thank you for the way you've supported me and the team this season. I've always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

"I'm grateful to the owners and Suhail [Shaikh, Blackburn's chief operating officer] for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will take responsibility of first-team duties, with Blackburn facing Burnley in the league on Saturday.

Some reports suggest that Mowbray has not stepped down from the role completely, meaning Blackburn are not thought to be looking for a successor.

#1837. Barcelona sweating over fitness of Pau Cubarsi for Villarreal clash after injury in Spain defeat

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 17:03, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 17:05

Barcelona have released a statement confirming that Pau Cubarsi picked up an injury during Spain's UEFA Nations League contest with England on Sunday night.

Cubarsi started the clash with the Three Lions but was substituted at the half-time break.

Barcelona have revealed that the centre-back has strained his hip flexor, but it is unclear at this stage of proceedings how long the 19-year-old could be on the sidelines.

“First-team player Pau Cubarsi has ​​a strain in his iliopsoas muscle. His availability for the match against Villarreal will depend on his recovery," read a statement from Barcelona.

Cubarsi has not yet been ruled out of Barcelona's La Liga clash with Villarreal on Sunday, but he is a doubt at this stage of proceedings.

The defender has been a vital player for Barcelona during the 2026-27 campaign, making 13 appearances in all competitions, providing two assists in the process.

Cubarsi will now not be in action with Spain until March, when the Nations League quarter-finals take place, with his full focus in the months ahead therefore set to be on Barcelona.

After the clash with Villarreal, Barcelona will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with an away fixture against Sabah on November 25.

Barcelona will then finish the move away to Deportivo La Coruna in La Liga, before beginning December with a clash against Atletico Madrid on December 2.

Hansi Flick's side beat Atletico 2-1 when the pair last met on November 8.

Jules Kounde remains on the sidelines through injury, and he is unlikely to be unavailable for the clash against Villarreal this weekend.

However, Eric Garcia made his return from a muscular injury against Atletico as a second-half substitute, and the Spain international will likely replace Cubarsi in the starting side against Villarreal, should the latter be unavailable for selection.

#1836. Man Utd transfer news: How much Fulham could demand for Calvin Bassey 'revealed'

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 17:14

Manchester United will reportedly need to pay a handsome fee to sign Fulham defender Calvin Bassey during the January transfer window.

Mauricio Pochettino is keen to shore up United's leaky defence, and Bassey has emerged as a strong candidate to strengthen his backline.

The centre-back has made more than 110 appearances for the Cottagers across all competitions, scoring four goals, and has featured nine times in the Premier League this season.

The Red Devils have been monitoring the 26-year-old for some time, and Pochettino's arrival has further strengthened the case for pursuing his signature.

According to TeamTalk, Manchester United would need to pay a fee in the region of £40m to bring Bassey to Old Trafford during the January transfer window.

Alvaro Arbeloa is keen for Bassey to commit his future to the club, and the Cottagers could potentially demand as much as £50m for their key centre-back.

Bassey's contract runs until the end of the season, and although Fulham have the option to extend it by another year, negotiations over a new deal have not progressed as smoothly as the club would have hoped.

The report claims that the former Rangers defender would be more than open to the prospect of moving to Old Trafford, which could work in Man Utd's favour.

Bassey would be an excellent addition to the squad and, in theory, should fit perfectly into Pochettino's system.

Pochettino typically favours an aggressive high defensive line, with pace and recovery speed essential qualities for his defenders, and Bassey certainly fits that profile.

Furthermore, the Nigerian international has considerable Premier League experience under his belt, while the reported asking price should fall within Man Utd's budget.

Bassey is also versatile enough to operate at left-back, which would be a major boost for Pochettino as the Red Devils look to provide cover for Luke Shaw.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Jurrien Timber and David Raya are set to commit their long-term futures to Arsenal.

The Gunners have made a push to agree new deals with the core of their Premier League-winning squad, as the club look to kick on and dominate domestically and in Europe.

It is an emphatic response to recent discussions on Raya potentially eyeing a move to Spain at the end of his current contract.

Speaking to Marca last month, Raya said: “I would love to play in La Liga one day. Right now, I’m very happy at Arsenal. But it’s true that I’d love to play in LaLiga one day. It’s a very competitive league.

Arteta, though, has been adamant that he wants Raya to remain at Arsenal in the seasons ahead.

“I think David has to play in Spain at some point… on the beach, with his friends in the summer,” Arteta said in response to Raya’s interview.

“But for the next few years he needs to play here for Arsenal.”

Arteta looks set to get his wish, with Raya joining Rice and Timber in ensuring he spends the prime years of his career at Arsenal.

#1832. Archie Gray and Hayden Hackney on Scotland's radar as Sebastien Pocognoli looks to tempt stars away from England

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:44 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:53 EST, 12 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli has revealed that Scotland are stepping up their efforts to persuade players who are eligible for England to wear Dark Blue.

While the Belgian is content with the group of players at his disposal, he admits he and the SFA are in dialogue with certain individuals who, potentially, could improve the squad.

It’s understood that Tottenham’s Archie Gray and Everton’s Hayden Hackney are among the names with whom there are ongoing discussions ahead of the Euro 2028 qualifiers next year.

Both players have represented England – the country in which they were born – at Under-21 level yet could still switch to Scotland through family connections.

‘I have had direct contact or indirect contact,’ the Belgian admitted when asked about similarly eligible players. ‘When I go to the direct contact, it’s because I feel it’s a first positive approach.

‘Yeah, I’ve done it with many players. I’ll do my best to bring them.’

Scotland boss Pocognoli is keen to add to his options and has spoken to potential new recruits

Under Steve Clarke, Scotland tried to persuade Harvey Barnes to switch allegiance only for the Newcastle player to confirm that he felt English.

Prepared to take each case on its merits, Pocognoli explained: ‘With Barnes it was different. The two other lads (Gray and Hackney) are young lads. It’s a long way. But if you wait too long, it might not be the right moment.

‘In a year’s time, we will see. Right now, we have players in the squad who are performing well.

‘It will always be up to them (current players) to be the priority because we’ve built things and we’ve had time with the ones who are here right now.’

While Pocognoli has previously made it clear that he won’t beg any player to pull on a Scotland shirt, he feels it’s incumbent on him and the SFA to gauge the feelings of players down south who could help his side.

‘We are on it,’ he stressed. ‘We are always proactive in all of these situations.

‘What is very exciting about those two names is that they are young players. That’s interesting.

Archie Gray's dad Andy, uncle Eddie and grandfather Frank all represented Scotland

‘We have to look and manage the situation. But it won’t be a definitive choice from them because we weren’t proactive. That has to be clear. We are proactive.

‘The best way to convince players is to show good football, show them they can come to us, enjoy it and be successful. They have to feel when they leave a top club that they arrive here into top conditions and a top environment.

‘That’s the best publicity we can offer, to show good football. In the end, it’s a human decision, a feeling.

‘I didn’t have that case. With my Italian blood, maybe I wasn’t that good! But I can understand the feeling of what it’s like to have to choose a country, with your background, family, football education and social circle.

‘So, it’s not easy. But it’s always a feeling from inside and I need to feel it. When I feel it, I’ll try to be on it.’

Hayden Hackney has impressed for Everton this season and has played for Scotland Under-21s

Meanwhile, Pocognoli believes a fully fit Kieran Tierney can have a major role to play in his new-look side.

While the preferred systems of his predecessors meant accommodating the Celtic man and Andy Robertson could be a conundrum, the 3-4-3 which the Belgian deploys seems better suited to fielding the pair at the same time.

With Tierney back in contention to face North Macedonia after pulling out of the last squad through injury, the manager said: ‘He will bring a different profile. He has a fantastic left foot and is an experienced player who knows the squad and knows what it means to play for Scotland. It is a big plus. He trained very well this week and is very focused.

‘He can play different positions. He can play left-back, he can play in the back three, as he has in the past. He plays left-back for Celtic, but in some games he has inverted. He can also bring some offensive attributes in the back three. We are lucky to have someone with that profile.

‘It is always a challenge to try to make all the players shine in the best shape possible. We have strong competition on the left side.

‘We have quality players. I will try to find the best balance and make everybody shine. If we can play Kieran and Andy in the same team if they are fit, it is a plus for the team.’

Kieran Tierney has been tipped to have a big impact for Scotland under Pocognoli

Pocognoli is desperate to secure his first victory at Hampden this evening having tasted defeat in his first two home games with Switzerland and Slovenia.

‘I haven’t really experienced Hampden yet and I’d like to,’ he said. ‘I was frustrated in the first game (against the Swiss) because I thought we started quite good in the first 10 minutes.

‘Then we know what happened (red card for Jack Hendry). In the last game, it was just disappointment.

‘It’s important that we play a consistent game and combine a good result with good football. If we play average and win, I’ll be happy with three points.

‘But the process is to play good football as well. It’s important that we excite the fans and we have the players for that. I hope that we deliver what we’ve worked on in the last four days.’

#1830. Vasco da Gama vs Internacional - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 16 Nov 2026 17:16

Copa Sudamericana hopefuls Vasco da Gama will be looking to move into the top half of the Brasileirao table when they welcome relegation-threatened Internacional to Estadio Sao Januario this midweek.

The hosts sit 11th with 44 points after 34 matches, below 10th-placed Sao Paulo on goal difference, while the visitors are 16th on 38 points, just one point above the drop zone, making this an important meeting for both sides.

Although Vasco have enjoyed a marginally better second half of the campaign compared to their first 19 league outings (W5, D5, L9), the Gigante da Colina only recently recorded their first back-to-back top-flight wins since enjoying three straight victories between mid-September and early October.

Pedro Emanuel's side came from behind to beat Atletico-PR 3-1 in Curitiba on November 4 before travelling to Arena Conda and securing a 2-0 victory over Chapecoense 10 days later, courtesy of Bruno Duarte.

Both results came either side of a Copa do Brasil semi-final exit at the hands of Palmeiras following a penalty loss after a 2-2 aggregate draw, although there is no getting away from the fact that Emanuel has overseen an impressive improvement since taking charge in July.

However, the Portuguese coach must find a better balance at both ends of the pitch with time running out, as his side have scored 45 goals and conceded 50 in the league this season, while an improvement at Sao Januario is also needed.

Vasco have won just one of their last three league home games (D1, L1), with their most recent outing ending in a 4-1 defeat to leaders Flamengo, although Wednesday's hosts have picked up a decent 27 points from 17 top-flight matches on home soil this season.

Internacional head into this encounter on the back of a dramatic 1-0 victory over Coritiba, courtesy of an Alerrandro stoppage-time penalty, a result that lifted the team from southern Brazil out of the relegation zone.

Eduardo Baptista's side have now won nine of their 34 league matches (D11, L14) this season, scoring 38 goals and conceding 42, while alternating between defeats and victories across their most recent four outings.

Chasing their first consecutive Brasileirao victories since back-to-back wins against Santos and Chapecoense in March, the Colorado must also contend with a poor away record that has seen them pick up just 15 points from an available 51 on the road this season while failing to take maximum points in any of their last four trips (D1, L3).

However, having recorded victories in six of their last nine matches against Vasco (D1, L2), including a 4-1 success in the reverse fixture, Inter should have some reason for optimism heading into this encounter.

Three of those triumphs have come in four of their last four visits to Sao Januario, although the Colorado suffered a 5-1 defeat on their most recent trip to the ground.

Vasco could again be without Thiago Mendes, Nuno Moreira, Santiago Sosa and Tche Tche, all of whom missed the recent victory over Chapecoense through fitness problems.

#1829. Five reasons England can win 2027 Nations League

England are one of the most likely teams to win the Nations League next summer, and after Sunday’s heroic 10-man win in Spain they will be speaking about their chances just as openly and brashly as that.

Having topped their group ahead of the world champions, they know they will face a group runner-up in March’s quarter-finals, and that could mean a tasty-looking two-legged tie against Belgium or Germany.

Their sights will be set further into the distance, though — June’s Nations League Finals, comprising of four teams, presenting a golden opportunity for England to win their first serious silverware since the 1966 World Cup. Here’s why they can do it…

This is something that has long been true of England and predates Thomas Tuchel’s time in charge. Of course, their tournament runs naturally tend to be brought to an end by top teams, but it so often against tougher opponents in previous knockout rounds or other competitions when England also produce their best football.

The Three Lions have often struggled to break down well-drilled teams who seek to defend deep against them — e.g. Ghana, Hungary or Slovenia — but teams that come out and take the game to them often bring out the best in England.

In 2026 alone, they have defeated Croatia three times out of three (13-3 on aggregate) as well as France, Erling Haaland’s Norway, and Mexico at the Estadio Azteca during the World Cup.

Then on Sunday came one of the finest victories in the national team’s 154-year history as they beat world champions Spain 3-2 in Madrid, the first time they had ever avoided defeat in a match against the team ranked No1 in the world.

Almost more so than the World Cup or European Championships, the Nations League guarantees regular meetings with the truly elite teams. England have proven they can unsettle and unpick the world’s very best.

Among reasons why England can win the Nations League in 2027, this one, more than any other, speaks for itself.

Discounting that barmy 6-4 third-place play-off win over France in which neither player started, England’s two best players scored 12 of the team’s World Cup 13 goals. And since returning for the new season, their levels have not dropped. According to the Gradient Sports’ model for overall performance, Bellingham has been the very best player across Europe’s top five leagues this term, with Kane not far behind in fifth.

Kane may now be 33 but is in the peak of his career and last month lifted the Ballon d’Or. And in Bellingham, England have a truly unique player, masterful at all aspects of the game and with a level of supreme self-belief that teases a similar self-assuredness out of those around him. England can win something while they have both in this imperious state.

For decades it has felt as though England’s midfield either did not possess enough genuine star quality, or did but was unable to function despite housing big names. Now, though, with Elliot Anderson, Declan Rice and Bellingham ahead of them, it seems England can at last dominate in the middle of the park and may no longer need to be solely reliant on counter-attacking when facing the world’s best sides.

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

When Rice missed the last international break, in came Alex Scott to partner Anderson and the balance produced helped to deliver a blistering 7-0 win in Rijeka, Croatia’s heaviest-ever defeat.

Back in came Rice this month and he and Anderson complemented each other superbly as all-action anchors in Madrid until Anderson’s sending off and England’s 10-man survival job. Up to the red card, England’s pass completion rate was better than Spain’s — almost unheard of.

England have embraced the Premier League and modern club football over the past eight years or so in order to become far more like a club team themselves, and the way Tuchel’s team is evolving just so happens to introduce a couple of club link-ups that are already improving on-field chemistry.

On the left, Lewis Hall of Newcastle United is making the left-back position his own. And further forward he can interchange with a player he knows very well indeed. Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon stepped up his game in an England shirt in 2026 and earned his move to Catalonia following three and a half years at Newcastle. It is clear they know each other’s games inside out.

The opposite flank has the potential to become all about Arsenal. Ben White scored England’s third against Spain and is well-placed to nail down the right-back position in 2027. Alongside him in England’s strongest XI would be the Three Lions’ best centre-back, Ezri Konsa, and in midfield, Rice. On the right wing, once back fit: Bukayo Saka. An Arsenal quartet playing with each other week in, week out would only help England’s coherence on the pitch.

Here is a factor not to be underestimated. Spain, Portugal and France will all join England among the eight quarter-finalists in March, but they have all won trophies in recent years.

England have been just about the most consistent team in international football not just in Europe but right across the world since Gareth Southgate’s team reached the 2018 World Cup semi-finals, and yet a succession of quite or very near misses has still left them without silverware. The years of hurt continue as winning the World Cup in 1966 becomes an ever-more distant memory.

It is the common view, though, that the greatest period in England’s men’s history is the one we are currently in, and a trophy of some sort at some point does feel an inevitability.

Bellingham, Kane and Tuchel all possess the self-confidence and courage England need to finally conquer that final mountain. Gordon and Rice share the same winning mentality. England are one of the very best teams in the world and have nothing to fear. And, crucially, they may want it just that little bit more.

#1826. Thomas Frank’s first words as Crystal Palace manager as contract details, appointment is confirmed

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 17:20, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 17:40

Crystal Palace have announced the appointment of Thomas Frank as their new head coach.

The 53-year-old arrives at Selhurst Park following the departure of predecessor Pierre Sage, who was sacked last Thursday after less than five months in charge.

Frank has put pen to paper on a contract that runs through to June 2029 and returns to management for the first time since he was dismissed by Tottenham Hotspur in February.

"It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic football club. I'm really, really looking forward to it,” Frank told Crystal Palace’s official website.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.”

Chairman Steve Parish added: “I’m delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace. He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club.

“I’m confident Thomas’ extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season.”

We are pleased to confirm the appointment of Thomas Frank as Manager ? ℹ️ https://t.co/2wUzZAGt4S https://t.co/zv2vMPGPFz

Over the summer, Frank opened up about using his break from management to his advantage before making the next step in his career.

"Football remains a huge part of who I am, and I have chosen to use this time productively. Over the coming months, besides spending time with family and friends, I will continue studying, observing and learning from other leaders both within sport and beyond it.

“Time away from the touchline is allowing me to broaden my perspective and gather insights that I look forward to bringing into my next challenge.

"When the time is right, I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication.”

That time is now with Crystal Palace, with Frank becoming the third manager to take charge of three different London clubs in the Premier League after Alan Pardew (Charlton, Crystal Palace, West Ham) and Harry Redknapp (QPR, Spurs, West Ham).

At Spurs, Frank won just 13 of his 38 games and left the club sitting down in 16th place in the Premier League table, five points above the relegation zone.

Before his brief spell in North London, Frank made his name as a first-team manager with Brentford where he enjoyed a successful seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025.

Frank guided the Bees to the Premier League after winning promotion from the Championship in 2020-21, and he established them as a competitive top-flight team that finished 13th, ninth, 16th and 10th across the following four campaigns, accumulating more than 50 points in three of those.

Across spells with Brentford and Spurs, Frank has won 61, drawn 46 and lost 71 of his 178 Premier League games as a manager (34.27% win ratio).

He is now tasked with steering new club Crystal Palace away from the relegation picture as the Eagles bid to shake off a disappointing start to the campaign and extend their 13-year stay in the Premier League.

Palace currently sit rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their first 10 games under Sage, but they could move out of the bottom three and up to 16th place if Frank wins his first game in charge away against Coventry City on Saturday.

Frank has plenty of rebuilding to do at Selhurst Park, with three key priorities sitting at the top of his in-tray.

#1825. Who is Silvia Tuya? New Manchester United female coach set to make history

Manchester United are set to make history with the appointment of Silvia Tuya as part of Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal revive Vinicius talks; Man Utd want Hall

Arsenal’s next two deals revealed after major contract breakthrough

Man Utd have already agreed a £9m compensation package with the US Soccer Federation to extract Pochettino from his contract as manager of the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT).

Following the Argentine to Old Trafford will be long-serving lieutenants, including assistant manager Jesus Perez and goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez.

But Pochettino will also bring newer additions to his coaching team, including strength and conditioning coach Tuya in what will be a first for Man United.

Silvia Tuya - full name Silvia Tuya Vinas - is a strength and conditioning coach, currently employed by the USMNT.

Tuya will become the first female coach of the men’s first team squad at Old Trafford, creating history ahead of a new chapter for Manchester United.

The strength and conditioning coach will be familiar with creating such history, having previously become the first female coach in the history of the USMNT’s senior squad when she joined the backroom staff in October 2024.

Tuya holds a doctorate of science in high performance and is fluent in English, Spanish, and Catalan.

She has previously lectured at the University of Barcelona and National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia, before joining Pochettino’s USA set up in October 2024.

Prior to the move to the States, the Spaniard briefly worked with FC Badalona in her native Catalonia, the team competing in Liga F - the top-flight of the women’s game in Spain.

Tuya also worked with Levante’s women's team, and has experience in strength and conditioning athletes from other disciplines, such as tennis, rugby, basketball, and ironman competitors.

The specialist in strength and conditioning was in charge of physical preparation at Levante, and will likely work closely with fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino - son of Mauricio - at Man United.

A PhD fellow, Tuya has contributed to different scientific papers, including research into reactions in football.

While certain members of Pochettino’s backroom staff have already travelled to England, the Guardian claim Tuya, analyst Alec Scott and Miguel D’Agostino have remained with the USA camp ahead of the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final second leg with Haiti.

As such, Tuya will be expected to start work at Carrington from November 18 - the same day as Pochettino.

Man United agreed that Pochettino could take charge of the USA’s games against Haiti before starting work at Carrington and Old Trafford.

#1824. Concerns as Arsenal Start Handing Out New Contracts

Arsenal’s willingness to hand new contracts to key figures such as Declan Rice, David Raya and Jurrien Timber is entirely understandable. These are not squad players being rewarded for loyalty; they are central pillars of a team that has developed into one of the strongest in Europe under Mikel Arteta. Reports indicate that Arsenal are moving towards new agreements with several of those players as they attempt to protect the core of the squad for the years ahead.

The challenge facing Arsenal is that successful teams eventually encounter a difficult balancing act. Keeping a title-winning squad together sounds attractive in theory, but football rarely allows clubs to stand still. At some stage, decisions have to be made about age profiles, wage structures and the next cycle of the team.

The next phase of Arsenal’s evolution could depend as much on who eventually leaves as who stays.

There is little debate around the wisdom of extending Rice’s contract. He has become one of the defining players of the Arteta era and is widely regarded as one of the Premier League’s outstanding midfielders. Timber’s importance has also grown significantly following his recovery from injury, while Raya has established himself as one of the league’s most reliable goalkeepers. Piero Hincapié, another player viewed as central to the club’s future, has reportedly signed a new deal already, though the club are yet to issue an official confirmation at the time of writing.

🚨 Piero Hincapie extends Arsenal stay by signing new & improved contract to remain at Emirates Stadium until summer 2032. Ecuador int’l previously committed to June 2031; fresh agreement adds 12mnths on improved salary rewarding #AFC status @TheAthleticFC https://t.co/d4742JTPbZ

— David Ornstein (@David_Ornstein) November 17, 2026

The logic behind these renewals is obvious. Arsenal have spent years building a squad capable of winning major honours. Allowing elite players to drift towards the final years of their contracts would create uncertainty and expose the club to unnecessary risk.

From a football perspective, securing the futures of those players is straightforward.

The complications arise when the wider picture is considered.

Much of Arsenal’s success has been built on careful squad construction. One of Arteta’s greatest achievements was creating a team that could improve together rather than peak at different times.

That process becomes more difficult when an increasing number of senior players move into their late twenties and early thirties simultaneously.

A cluster of important Arsenal players have contracts which expire in 2028, including Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Ben White, Mikel Merino, Declan Rice, David Raya and Jurrien Timber. Many are either already in their peak years or approaching them.

There is a natural temptation to keep extending deals and retain a successful group. The danger is that a squad can age faster than expected. What appears sensible in 2026 can look problematic by 2029 if too many key players are on expensive long-term contracts at the same stage of their careers.

Elite clubs constantly refresh, they evolve while remaining competitive. Such an approach requires difficult judgment calls.

Supporters naturally focus on the stars they want to keep, but executives are forced to think differently.

Every new contract impacts the wage bill. Every long-term commitment affects future flexibility. Every decision made for one player influences negotiations with others. If Rice receives terms comparable to Arsenal’s highest earners, as has been reported, it will inevitably shape expectations across the dressing room.

That does not mean Arsenal should avoid rewarding their best performers. Quite the opposite. The club are right to secure the futures of players they believe can form the backbone of the team for years to come.

It does mean there will eventually come a point where not everybody can receive the same treatment. Some contracts will be extended, others may not. That is the reality of long-term squad planning.

For now, Arsenal’s contract activity should be viewed as a sign of strength rather than concern. Clubs in decline rarely spend their time trying to protect the futures of their most important players. Arsenal are doing so because they remain convinced that the current project has room to grow.

The more intriguing question is what happens next.

Arteta has already built a team capable of winning the Premier League and challenging for the Champions League. Sustaining that level for another five years may require a different skill altogether. It will require the ability to refresh the squad without weakening it, identify the next generation before the current one begins to decline and make unpopular decisions before they become obvious.

Those decisions are rarely celebrated when they are made – they are usually only appreciated years later; if ever.

Arsenal are entering that phase now. Keeping Rice, Raya and Timber appears straightforward. The real challenge will be determining which members of this successful squad remain part of the next cycle, and which make way for it.

#1823. Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: 'Truth' revealed regarding club's 'interest' in Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 17:30, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 17:33

Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe were reportedly both initially considered by Manchester United as potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but the club ultimately went in a different direction.

Mauricio Pochettino will officially begin work as Man United head coach on Thursday, with the Argentine agreeing to replace Carrick at Old Trafford.

Carrick was sacked by the 20-time English champions last week due to the team's struggles in the opening months of the 2026-27 campaign.

Conte and Howe have both been heavily linked with the role in recent weeks; the former is available immediately following his exit from Napoli at the end of last season, while the latter departed Newcastle United ahead of the 2026-27 Premier League campaign.

According to The Athletic, Man United's minority shareholder Sir Jim Ratcliffe had been keen on exploring a move for Conte given his credentials.

The report claims that Conte was interested in the position at Old Trafford, with representatives contacting Man United to make that point clear.

However, some senior figures at Old Trafford did not believe that Conte was the right fit at this moment in time, with the club going through a difficult period.

The 57-year-old was in charge of Chelsea between July 2016 and July 2018, winning the Premier League title and FA Cup at Stamford Bridge, and he then managed Tottenham Hotspur between November 2021 and March 2023.

As a result, a move to Man United would have equalled a third spell in the Premier League.

Howe, meanwhile, has taken charge of Bournemouth, Burnley and Newcastle United during his management career, and his vast experience in the Premier League placed him in the running.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox is believed to have pushed Howe's name into the conversation, but 'the matter did not progress further', while it is understood that the 48-year-old was 'left off the final names considered'.

The Athletic insist that a move to Man United for Howe was never at an advanced stage despite the recent reports.

Former France manager Didier Deschamps was allegedly contacted over the position, but discussions with the Frenchman's representatives are not believed to have been positive.

#1822. Tottenham starting to carve out new identity under Roberto De Zerbi as rest of season predicted

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

After a tricky start to the season, Tottenham have begun to find their feet under Roberto De Zerbi.

Despite spending more than £300million on new players over the summer, Spurs were bottom of the Premier League table before the September international break.

They have since found form, though, losing just one of their next five games and, after an unbeaten October, De Zerbi was crowned Premier League Manager of the Month last week.

Spurs endured a nightmare opening weekend as their expensively assembled squad was dismantled 3-0 by Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Performances have since improved, though, and Spurs produced a result for the ages when they beat Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge to secure just their second win in 42 attempts at the Blues’ home ground.

Defeat to Leeds in their last game was a setback, but overall performances have steadily evolved, and Spurs are starting to carve out an identity under De Zerbi.

Spurs embarked on a comprehensive squad overhaul during the summer as they parted ways with a number of senior players while also looking to build a team in De Zerbi’s image.

The addition of centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke, who worked under De Zerbi at Brighton, has proven an astute piece of business, and he has begun to develop a solid partnership with fellow Dutch international Micky van de Ven.

In midfield, Spurs went big, splashing £185m on Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali. The pair have taken a bit of time to acclimatise, but recently they have begun to develop an understanding with each other.

There is still a lot more to come, though, from Spurs’ attacking signings, with Savio and Mykhailo Mudryk struggling for fitness while striker Omar Marmoush has flattered to deceive since arriving from Manchester City.

Having guided Spurs to Premier League survival last season, De Zerbi has plenty of goodwill in the bank, and it is why his job didn’t come under serious scrutiny when Spurs failed to win any of their first five league games.

The Italian’s substitutions have drawn criticism, and Spurs still struggle to react to going behind, but overall De Zerbi has his team playing with intensity and personality.

Issues still persist in attack, but that is as much down to personnel as it is De Zerbi’s tactics. Either way, though, he will have to find a way to make Spurs more efficient in the final third.

#1819. Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal triple deal, Vinicius talks; Man Utd eye Hall; Chelsea, Liverpool latest

The January transfer window is approaching, with Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham all considering moves to strengthen their squads for the second half of the season. Arsenal are among the clubs interested in Como midfielder Nico Paz, although they face competition from Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain. Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi and RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa are also admired at the Emirates Stadium, while Juventus midfielder Kenan Yildiz is another player on Mikel Arteta’s radar as he looks to reinforce his attacking options.

Mauricio Pochettino was appointed Manchester United manager last week, replacing Michael Carrick, and could make Calvin Bassey his first signing. The former Chelsea boss is keen to strengthen a defence that has struggled this season, with the Fulham defender potentially providing a solution. Pochettino will face the media ahead of United’s meeting with Aston Villa as preparations continue.

Chelsea are confident of securing a deal for Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott when the window opens, despite the Cherries insisting he is not for sale. Liverpool are also monitoring young talent, with Mexican midfielder Gilberto Mora among their targets. The Reds are additionally interested in Lamine Camara, who came close to joining Chelsea on deadline day during the summer transfer window. Follow all the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Manchester United transfer target Yasin Ayari appeared to pour cold water on any potential move to Old Trafford - before implying that he is keeping his options open.

Ayari has been a key part of Brighton’s bright start to the Premier League campaign, hitting three goals in nine appearances.

Ayari is out of contract this summer leading to speculation regarding his future. United are said to be among the clubs keeping an eye on his situation.

They are far from the only club credited with an interest in the 23-year-old, though. Premier League leaders Arsenal, Serie A outfit Roma, and Turkish duo Fenerbahce and Galatasaray are all reported to be keeping tabs on the Swede.

But, speaking from the Swedish national team camp this week, Ayari appeared to play down reports linking him with a move away from the AmEx: “I’m at Brighton and I’m happy where I am. Things are going well for me right now. Then we’ll see what’s to come.”

JJ Gabriel has confirmed his decision to leave Manchester United in a statement, with Real Madrid expected to win the race to sign the highly-rated young winger.

The 16-year-old has played in United’s academy since 2020 and was expected to start appearing in the first team this season.

Until, that is, he made the shock decision to lodge a transfer request in September, amid reports he and his entourage were frustrated with his lack of first-team opportunities.

United worked hard to convince him to stay and offered him a new contract, but the player has not trained at the club for some time and is now expected to join Real Madrid. He will leave Old Trafford without having made a senior appearance.

After months of speculation as to where he might end up, Gabriel has now issued the clearest update yet on his situation, confirming his decision to leave United in a post to his Instagram page.

Speaking over clips of himself playing for the club, he said: “Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams.

“Here, I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award, you gave me moments I’ll always treasure.

“To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

“As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ.”

Just in from the BBC, Arsenal in advanced talks with Piero Hincapie over a contract extension on improved terms.

Furthermore, discussions over new deal for Riccardo Calafiori are on the horizon.

Busy period at the home of the Premier League champions.

QPR youngster Leon Scarlett is attracting interest from Eintracht Frankfurt and AC Milan after breaking into the first team this season, writes Sam Tabuteau.

Scarlett, who can play on the left and right wing, has made six Championship appearances for high-flying QPR after joining the club on a scholarship deal from Arsenal’s academy last summer.

The 17-year-old has already been capped by Wales at Under-21 level, and Standard Sport understands several clubs in England and Europe have registered an interest.

Manchester United are set to make history with the appointment of Silvia Tuya as part of Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff.

Man Utd have already agreed a £9m compensation package with the US Soccer Federation to extract Pochettino from his contract as manager of the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT).

Following the Argentine to Old Trafford will be long-serving lieutenants, including assistant manager Jesus Perez and goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez.

But Pochettino will also bring newer additions to his coaching team, including strength and conditioning coach Tuya in what will be a first for Man United.

George Hemmings is staying at Aston Villa!

Manchester United should sign Chelsea youngster Estevao, says former defender Mikael Silvestre.

The 19-year-old has made 46 appearances for the Blues since arriving in London last summer from Palmeiras for an initial £29million deal.

Estevao, however, has been handed just one Premier League start by new Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso so far this season - coincidentally against Man United last month.

The Brazilian would go on to impress, helping his side seal a 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge, a result that increased the pressure on then-head coach Michael Carrick who has since been sacked and replaced by Mauricio Pochettino.

Declan Rice has agreed a new long-term contract with Arsenal, writes Matt Verri.

The midfielder began talks with the club over improved terms earlier in the year and those have accelerated in recent weeks.

It is understood that a verbal agreement has now been reached and Rice will soon put pen to paper on the deal.

Newcastle have no intention of selling Lewis Hall in January despite growing interest in the England international.

The 22-year-old has established himself as Thomas Tuchel’s first-choice left-back following impressive performances against Croatia and Spain, attracting attention from clubs across Europe.

Manchester United made an approach for Hall last summer but were told he was not for sale, before the defender signed a new long-term contract in September.

According to The Telegraph, Newcastle are likely to demand well over £80m for a defender contracted until 2031.

Barcelona, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain could also emerge as potential suitors.

Arsenal are increasingly confident they can sign Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr in 2027, despite the Brazilian recently extending his contract at the Spanish club until 2032.

According to FootballTransfers, the Gunners still view the 26-year-old as their leading target to strengthen the left wing, with senior figures believing a deal could be possible as early as next summer.

Vinicius has struggled for consistency this season and faces competition from new signing Yan Diomande for a starting place.

Arsenal reportedly believe they remain an attractive destination after the forward seriously considered their offer last summer. However, any move is unlikely before next summer, with the club prepared to be patient in their pursuit.

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 17:43

Liverpool would reportedly love to sign Ronald Araujo permanently from Barcelona following a series of impressive performances since his arrival at Anfield.

Araujo joined the Reds on loan from La Liga giants Barcelona, with the Merseyside club holding an option to make his move permanent for £47m.

The Uruguay international had struggled during the past couple of seasons at the Catalan club, making the switch a potentially beneficial move for all parties involved.

So far, the 27-year-old defender has proved to be an excellent addition, making 10 Premier League appearances and starting eight of them.

It has previously been reported that the Reds are considering signing Araujo permanently following his impressive start to life at Anfield.

With Conor Bradley sidelined, Araujo has done an excellent job filling the void at right-back, while he has also featured as a centre-back under Andoni Iraola.

According to Marca, Liverpool would happily make his move permanent right now, but they can only activate the option at the end of the season.

Araujo is said to be happy at Liverpool, but the Reds are taking a cautious approach to the defender's situation in case he suffers an injury or experiences a significant dip in form.

Liverpool will need to recruit a new centre-back, and potentially another right-back, next season, making Araujo an appealing option.

Having spent an entire season working under Iraola, the defender should also have a much better understanding of the manager's tactical demands.

At the same time, much will depend on where Liverpool finish the campaign and whether their final league position influences their transfer plans.

Araujo still has several good years of football ahead of him, but the Reds may be tempted to invest the money in promising young talent or use it to bring Jarell Quansah back to Anfield.

#1817. Calafiori enjoying ‘best moment of my career’ at Arsenal

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Riccardo Calafiori believes he is having the "best moment of my career" for Arsenal after being honoured by Rome Mayor Roberto Gualtieri on Tuesday.

The full-back was presented with a special plaque in his hometown for "the outstanding results achieved" in 2026, which included Arsenal's first Premier League title since 2003-04.

Calafiori made 36 appearances in all competitions last season, with 26 of those coming in the Premier League.

He also helped Arsenal to reach the EFL Cup and Champions League finals, though the Gunners suffered defeat on both occasions, to Manchester City and Paris Saint-Germain respectively.

Calafiori, who joined Arsenal in July 2024, has also impressed at the start of 2026-27, scoring two goals and registering two assists in 12 appearances so far.

"I want to thank Mayor Gualtieri. I felt quite emotional walking in here," Calafiori told reporters via Football Italia.

"Thank you for this recognition, which fills me with pride. I always try to represent my Roman roots abroad. Whenever I come back, it's always a great emotion."

"I think it's the best moment of my career," he added about his spell at Arsenal.

"I feel like a leader in the dressing room, and I try to help my team-mates and the younger players."

A post shared by Riccardo Calafiori (@richycala)

Calafiori started his career at Roma, coming through the academy and making his first-team debut in 2020 before leaving to join Basel in August 2022.

He made just 10 appearances for Roma, and the Italian has confirmed he would like to return to the Giallorossi at some point in the future.

"I hope to win as much as possible over the coming years," he added.

"Then, in the more distant future, as I've always said, I would love to return to Roma.

"Everyone speaks highly of [Gian Piero] Gasperini and his ability to get the best out of players. I hope he can achieve the best possible results by the end of the season."

#1814. Hull injury news: Nobel Mendy update on “problem” ahead of Brighton Premier League clash

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 17:58

Hull City defender Nobel Mendy has emerged as an injury doubt ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash with Brighton & Hove Albion.

The £21m summer signing from Rayo Vallecano was called up to Patrick Vieira’s Senegal squad this month ahead of a double-header against Sudan in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.

Mendy watched on as an unused substitute for Senegal’s 4-1 home win over Sudan last Thursday, but he was not selected in the matchday squad for their 4-2 away victory on Monday.

Vieira has confirmed that Mendy was sent back to Hull from international duty with a suspected knee injury following an examination by Senegal’s medical team.

He told reporters: “[Mendy] felt a problem with his knee, so after consulting with our medical staff and his club’s medical team, we decided not to take any risks and to let him return to his club.”

Vieira added: “We hope it’s not too serious and that he can play again as soon as possible.”

The fact that Mendy’s problem is “not too serious” provides Hull with hope that he could feature in some capacity against Brighton at the MKM Stadium this weekend.

A new update on his condition is set to be provided by Tigers head coach Sergej Jakirovic at his pre-match press conference on Friday.

Mendy dealt with a few fitness issues at the start of the season before a nasty blow to the head in a 2-2 draw with Chelsea in mid-September saw him rushed to hospital.

The defender was diagnosed with concussion and subsequently missed the 2-1 defeat at Newcastle United, before returning to play his first full 90 minutes of the season in a 2-2 home draw with Everton after the September/October international break.

Mendy was then sidelined for back-to-back league games against Fulham and Brentford due to a groin injury, but he was fit to return for matches against Ipswich Town and Arsenal.

Should Mendy not recover in time to face Brighton, Lucas Herrington would be the most likely candidate to start in his place alongside John Egan and Semi Ajayi in a three-man defence.

Elsewhere on the injury front, Charlie Hughes played his first game of the season for Hull Under-21s last week and may be in a position to return to the first-team fold this weekend.

Mohamed Belloumi (thigh), Hidemasa Morita (groin) and Ilyas Ansah (back) will all have injuries assessed ahead of the Brighton clash, but Eliot Matazo (knee) and Matt Targett (ankle) remain sidelined.

#1813. Bruno Guimaraes assists Vinicius Junior after Arsenal transfer plans ‘revealed’

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes claimed yet another assist for Vinicius Junior, with the Real Madrid forward rediscovering his goalscoring touch.

Vinicius Jr scored a hat-trick as Brazil thumped Singapore 7-0 in a friendly on Tuesday morning, following up on his brace in the 3-2 defeat to Japan on Saturday.

An impressive tally of five goals in two games during a successful international break may prove a turning point in the season for the 26-year-old after admitting his form for Real Madrid had been impacted by summer links to Arsenal.

“I don’t think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup, because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians,” Vinicius Jr said.

“Being knocked out so early was something we hadn’t expected. So, I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in previous years.

“That may have affected my start to the season. On top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid. But it’s a very long season.”

Interestingly, perhaps, of Vinicius Jr’s five goals across the two games, three of them were created by Bruno Guimaraes.

The Arsenal midfielder assisted both goals against Japan and then repeated the trick inside the opening 10 minutes against Singapore with a fine pass - though Vinicius’ first touch did make the opportunity even easier.

The connection between Guimaraes and Vinicius Jr in recent days has prompted chatter on social media among some Arsenal fans about revisiting a deal for the latter at some point in 2027.

That said, reports claim the Gunners still view the 26-year-old as their leading target to strengthen the left wing, with senior figures believing a deal could be possible as early as next summer.

#1812. Alfie Whiteman interview: Life is short, I left Tottenham and football to experience the world

From the Europa League final to the Prince Charles Cinema, the former goalkeeper is carving out a new career

Trawl through Alfie Whiteman’s most recent Instagram post, and you will stumble across a fridge cluttered with magnets, polaroid pictures and a Europa League winners medal.

There, hidden within a carousel of charity shops, cameras and cats, lies a perfectly understated summation of where football figures for a man who cut short his professional career at just 26, not through injury or mental distress, but to pursue a passion for the arts.

Whiteman spent 16 years as a goalkeeper at his boyhood club, Tottenham, but he admits he has not been back to watch them live since hanging up his gloves in October last year.

“I had an offer,” Whiteman tells Standard Sport after taking part in a live Q&A for the launch of Together Tottenham - a new shared mission between the club and Spurs in the Community to create 150,000 meaningful opportunities for local young people by 2030.

Life is short, and I wanted to make sure I experienced the other wonderful things the world has to offer

“I could have continued to play, but I think for many years prior I was always planning for life after (football).

“Life is short, and I wanted to make sure I experienced the other wonderful things the world has to offer, but it was a huge decision that came with a lot of self-doubt and risk because there wasn’t something set up for me to look into.”

Whiteman stepped into the unknown in pursuit of his “purpose beyond the sport”. But it is a decision he is grateful he took after years spent living a “double life” in which his creative instincts were “discouraged”.

Physically and metaphorically, he had closed the door on his football career, locking away his Europa League and 2019 Champions League runners-up medal in a drawer before eventually putting them pride of place alongside pictures of his friends and family.

He continued: “It’s funny. For a long time they (the medals) were just in a drawer, but I thought I’d put them out as a reminder for me of all the wonderful experiences that my life and football gave me and how hard I worked.

“My whole childhood was essentially devoted to battling my way through the footballing system, which famously is not an easy one to go through.”

Whiteman only ever made one senior competitive appearance for Spurs, coming on as an 82nd-minute substitute for Joe Hart in a 4–0 Europa League win against Ludogorets Razgrad in November 2020.

However, his connection to the club remains strong, and he admits the 2025 Europa League triumph against Manchester United, which ended Spurs’ 17-year wait for a major trophy, was the perfect send-off.

“I look back on it as the best possible final game, running on that pitch and celebrating with my wonderful teammates and all the work we put in through a tricky year.”

Despite winning the Europa League, it was a complicated campaign for Spurs, as they slumped to their worst ever Premier League season, finishing 17th and losing 22 of their 38 league games.

Spurs dropped everything to end their trophy drought, and manager Ange Postecoglu paid with his job, sacked 16 days after the final despite staying true to his promise to deliver silverware in his second season.

Simultaneously “within and without” as the Great Gatsby narrator, Nick Carraway, once famously quipped, Whiteman held a unique position in Spurs’ squad during his final season.

People think they know a lot about [football] but the reality of it within the walls of the training ground is probably quite different

He was aware he was never likely to influence the game on the pitch, yet understood he had a role to play in the dressing room and on the training ground as they stood on the cusp of history.

“I do feel football is something that people think they know a lot about but the reality of it within the walls of the training ground is probably quite different,” Whiteman asserts. “Everyone wins together and suffers together.”

Retirement was already in Whiteman’s plans as he rushed onto the pitch in Bilbao. Four years earlier, he captured over 600 vulnerable self-portraits and diary entries that encapsulated the solitude, loneliness, and self-exploration of his loan spell with Swedish club Degerfors IF.

These insights would form the basis of his first formal step into the arts, as his exhibition ‘A Loan’ was showcased at the OOF Gallery inside the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

“It wasn’t a project made with the idea of it being exhibited. It was purely out of this time of searching for purpose, frustration with self, feeling like I’m down a path that maybe isn’t the one I want to do and dealing with insecurities and imposter syndrome.

“It was just reflecting upon all those things of self-doubt, so it was quite surreal, actually. It was nice that it was resonating with people.”

Influenced by his parents, who were always “encouraging art and expression”, and his upbringing in cosmopolitan London, Whiteman is also a major film buff and regularly heads to the BFI Southbank or the Prince Charles Cinema in Leicester Square.

He recently attended the BFI’s London Film Festival, where the comedy-drama Club Kid was among the screenings to catch his attention. If there was one film to sum up his time at Spurs, though?

“Wow, that’s a tricky question,” he chuckles before a clinical concentration becomes etched across his face as if stepping up to save the winning penalty in the World Cup final.

“Wim Wenders’ (1987 romantic fantasy) Wings of Desire but maybe (Wenders’ 2023 Japanese-language drama) Perfect Days, one of his more recent films.

“I think (in Perfect Days) it was this real appreciation of life itself and the small things, and not getting caught up in all the stresses we have and just taking a step back and appreciating how lucky we are, which I think that film really encapsulates.

“It’s about really finding purpose in what you’re doing, and that sort of beauty of the small everyday things.”

#1810. Mauricio Pochettino's plan of action 'revealed' as new Man United manager's assistants head to Manchester to begin preparations for Liverpool

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 18:07, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 18:11

Mauricio Pochettino will reportedly be ready to start work as Manchester United head coach on Wednesday morning, with the Red Devils arranging a private jet for the Argentine to head to England once his duties with the USA have concluded.

Man United appointed Pochettino as their new head coach on Friday, but he has not yet arrived in Manchester, having agreed to take charge of USA's two matches during this international period against Haiti.

The United States beat Haiti 6-0 in the first leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final on November 14, with the second leg taking place at midnight on Tuesday UK time.

According to the Daily Mail, Man United have arranged a private jet which will see Pochettino land in England on Wednesday morning ready to begin work.

The report claims that the 54-year-old will speak to the media and then say goodbye to his players before heading to Manchester; he will therefore sleep on the plane and be ready to head straight to Carrington to begin work.

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino have already travelled to Manchester.

First-team coach Miguel D’Agostino and fitness coach Silvia Tuya are set to follow.

"The assistants are ahead. After the game they flew to Manchester and they are there in advance," Pochettino told reporters on Monday.

"That was the plan when we agreed terms with Manchester United and with the national team. They are there in advance. They are preparing because Wednesday when we will arrive it’s going to be non-stop, and then start with playing games."

Pochettino's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions will be Sunday's Premier League clash against Liverpool at Anfield.

Man United will then head to Portugal at the start of next week to prepare for their Champions League contest with Sporting Lisbon on November 25.

Pochettino is expected to speak to the media at Carrington on Friday afternoon, where he will also be asked for a team news update ahead of the game with Liverpool.

#1809. Mikel Arteta has Arsenal stars looking as hungry as ever with rest of season predicted

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal hold a five-point lead at the top of the Premier League table.

A 3-0 loss at the Amex Stadium against Brighton was the only one of their ten matches so far this season in which they have dropped points in the league.

With 10 points from a possible 12 in the Champions League as well, it has been near enough as good a start as Mikel Arteta and his players could have wished for.

The defeat away at Brighton was a horror show and the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood was embarrassing, but otherwise it was a superb start to the season for Arsenal.

They have, on the whole, played better football than last season, even if many matches have not had the margin to make it feel more comfortable.

Arsenal went toe-to-toe with Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena, a performance that should give them real confidence when the knockout stages of the Champions League come around.

It has been a tough run of fixtures to start the season, with so many difficult away trips already ticked off, and Arsenal have come through that sitting pretty.

Ezri Konsa has been by far the standout of the summer additions. He has slotted into the defence seamlessly and made an already formidable backline look effectively impenetrable.

There can be no greater compliment to Konsa than the fact he has given Arteta a major selection headache now William Saliba is fit again.

Bruno Guimaraes' best moments have come off the bench, with goals against Sunderland and Leeds. He has thrived when things have been more desperate and there is a chaotic edge to the match.

When starting alongside Declan Rice, Guimaraes has looked far less comfortable and his lack of mobility has been exposed on several occasions.

Further up the pitch, Christos Tzolis made a bright start to life at the club before missing a month with a hamstring injury.

It is still hard not to look at the summer transfer window as a huge missed opportunity in attack. Arsenal needed to do much more.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea have made progress under Xabi Alonso in some areas but in others still look the same chaotic team Enzo Maresca and then Liam Rosenior presided over.

They sit fifth in the table at present and boast one of the Premier League’s most thrilling attacks yet have also dropped points against Hull and lost to both Tottenham and Sunderland, who were bottom of the table at the time.

As the November international break draws to a close, it is time to reassess the progress they have made and the direction of travel under Alonso.

Chelsea’s season began with strong form but in truth has very much been a mixed bag so far.

The victories over Fulham, Brighton, Bournemouth and Leeds (in the Carabao Cup) have shown Chelsea at their free-flowing best, but only twice have they kept a Premier League clean sheet so far and there are defensive weaknesses that either need solving or, failing that, disguising by Alonso and his team in the months ahead.

The penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool that saw Chelsea exit the Carabao Cup early was a real disappointment in a season when there is no European football to be had, and it is understandable why plenty of Chelsea fans remain unsure quite what Alonso’s team are and what they want to be, even though they sit fifth in the league.

They have been beaten by Tottenham and Sunderland, neither of which should be games they are losing.

Chelsea made 10 first-team signings in the summer as they totally revamped their squad ready for Alonso’s first season in charge.

By far the best performer among their summer recruits has been Morgan Rogers, who has 11 goal contributions in 13 games for the Blues since his £117million arrival from Aston Villa during the World Cup.

Even though they failed to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco on deadline day, they did make other recruitments that have looked like proving shrewd signings, including Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria, Jordan Henderson and Maxence Lacroix.

#1806. Everton transfer news: Jack Grealish replacement emerges with Toffees among ‘top contenders’ for 21 G/A winger

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 18:19

Everton have identified Flamengo winger Samuel Lino as a possible transfer target, according to a report.

The Toffees are expected to bolster their squad in the January after enduring a frustrating end to the summer transfer window, selling Iliman Ndiaye, Beto and Tim Iroegbunam on Deadline Day without bringing in a replacement.

While the addition of a new centre-forward to ease the burden on Thierno Barry is thought to be among Everton’s main priorities, pursuing a new winger may also be high on the agenda for manager David Moyes.

The long-term future of Manchester City loanee Jack Grealish has come under the spotlight following his ‘breach of club discipline’ prior to the international break.

Tyrique George has since stepped up in Grealish’s absence on the left flank, while fellow wingers Brennan Johnson and Tyler Dibling have struggled to reach the heights expected on a consistent basis for some time.

According to Swiss news outlet 4-4-2, via the Liverpool Echo, Everton are among a number of 'top contenders' in the race to sign Brazil international Lino, along with Paris Saint-Germain, Juventus and Napoli.

The report adds that Roma – who along with Everton are owned by The Friedkin Group – recently saw a €25m (£20.9m) offer for Lino rejected by Flamengo.

Lino has established himself as a prolific winger with Flamengo this season, scoring 12 goals and providing nine assists in 33 Brazilian Serie A appearances.

The 26-year-old was not called up to Brazil’s squad for the November international break, but he did represent Carlo Ancelotti’s side last month and scored his first two goals from his country in a 4-0 friendly win over India.

Lino is thriving in his homeland having previously spent five-and-a-half years in Europe with Gil Vicente, Atletico Madrid and Valencia.

After scoring 23 goals in 100 games for Portuguese side Gil Vicente, Lino made the move to Atletico in July 2022 before spending a season on loan at Valencia, chipping in with eight goals and three assists in 41 matches.

Lino was then integrated into Diego Simeone’s Atletico side and made 65 La Liga appearances across two seasons, but he opted to return to Brazil in January 2025, joining Flamengo for a then club-record €22m (£18.4m) and signing a four-year contract.

With several big European clubs said to be interested in Lino, the winger may be tempted by a return to Europe heading into the prime years of his career.

Meanwhile, Everton are reportedly ready to battle fellow Premier League side Nottingham Forest for a £12.5m-rated centre-back from Brazil.

#1805. When I overtook Jim Leighton, that was when I started to wind Kenny up about beating his cap tally... ANDY ROBERTSON on going level with Dalglish

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:28 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 18:04 EST, 12 November 2026

It's a story which extols the virtues of loyalty and leadership in the proper sense.

More than anything, though, Andy Robertson’s achievements in football are – and always will be – reminders of what’s possible when a talented individual takes rejection as their motivation to redefine themselves in the eyes of the world.

Even though it’s been told many times before, the tale of the full-back’s determination to bounce back from being shown the door as a teenager by Celtic will never grow old.

Without having the character to overcome such adversity, he would not have been caught in the safety net at Queen’s Park. There would have been no moves to Dundee United and Hull. No Champions League and title-winning medals from his time with Liverpool. No first cap for his country.

In terms of a life lesson for those aspiring footballers who may find themselves in a cul-de-sac in their own careers, it has few equals.

All being well, Robertson will make his 102nd appearance for Scotland against North Macedonia, equalling the record tally of his idol and great friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish.

Andy Robertson will go level with Kenny Dalglish as Scotland's record cap holder on Friday

Both men are proud Glaswegians and Scots who bonded throughout their time together at Anfield. Dalglish would be the first to admit, though, that their respective paths have been distinct.

With a God-given talent so bright it could blind you, Dalglish was a superstar in the making before he wore a Scotland jersey for the first time against Belgium in 1971.

Coming in a friendly in Poland in 2014, Robertson’s first appearance only arrived after those early struggles.

It took huge character for him to even get that far. To add a century more across a dozen years under four different managers is a gargantuan achievement.

Football has a funny habit of throwing up strange co-incidences. Yesterday happened to be 40 years to the day since Dalglish won the last of his caps in a 3-0 win over Luxembourg.

Characteristically, before he took his own walk down memory lane, the man who’ll join him on that mark this evening was at pains to give the Anfield icon his rightful place.

‘It’s not really about me,’ Robertson insisted. ‘For how long the record stood, for starters, for what he (Dalglish) achieved in his career, for the person he is... tomorrow is another reason for our country to honour one of the greatest players that has played a game. He’s definitely the greatest in Scotland.

Dalglish scored 30 goals in his 102 caps and is regarded as Scotland's greatest ever player

‘Obviously, in terms of the number, I will stand side by side with him. But I don’t want people to forget how important this man has been to our country.

‘Because, for me, he was arguably the best player in the world at one time and will always be the greatest in this country, no matter what happens in the future.

‘He’ll always be the first one to do X, Y and Z. I just think that shouldn’t be forgotten.

‘Tomorrow is definitely a reason to do that for Kenny.’

There is, though, still no understating what Robertson has achieved across 12 years. Playing for Scotland wasn’t always the joy that it’s been in more recent times.

‘We get looked after so well off the pitch,’ he offered. ‘That probably wasn’t always the case when I first came in.

‘Under Gordon (Strachan) in my first qualifying campaign, I think I was still young enough to not think too much about it. But then I also remember under Alex McLeish and then the start of Steve Clarke, there was a real disconnect between the country and the players.

‘There wasn’t too much love for the players. We were getting 10,000, 15,000 inside Hampden. That was the most difficult time, especially as captain and being at Liverpool as well.’

He stuck at it and never shirked responsibility. In time he was able to chalk up the numbers because the side steadily improved and broke through the glass ceiling.

Robertson shares a laugh with Nathan Patterson ahead of the visit of North Macedonia

‘Of course, I would be sitting here with a few less caps if we hadn’t been successful,’ he reflected. ‘The fact that we got to two Euros, a World Cup and all the warm-up games and things like that resulted in me having an extra maybe 15 caps.

‘What makes it more special to me is the fact that we’ve managed to achieve things.’

All of this was beyond his wildest dreams at the beginning. A late substitute for Barry Bannan in a friendly in Warsaw on March 5, 2014, he can still hear Gordon Strachan whispering in his ear.

‘He basically said, “Don’t be scared, don’t go into your shell”,’ he recalled. ‘He said, “The reason I’ve picked you is because you’re brave. I see you bombing up and down the pitch for Dundee United”. He said, “Go and be that player”.

‘I always remember the first ball came to me and the words were ringing in my ears. I think I carried it 30 yards forward. It gave me the confidence to just go and try and play exactly the way I was playing under Jackie McNamara.’

Four years later, by then a Liverpool player, Robertson was handed the armband by McLeish following Scott Brown’s retirement.

‘That made me grow up and made me realise what it took to become a leader,’ he reflected. ‘I kind of grew into it. I believe that I became the captain that I wanted to be.’

It was only when he equalled McLeish’s 77 appearances that the prospect of one day equalling or surpassing Dalglish entered his head.

‘I think everyone in the room and everyone who personally knows me well enough knows that personal achievements aren’t really what I focus on,’ he said. ‘But I would lie if I said this wasn’t one that I’ve chased.

Like Dalglish, Robertson is a Liverpool icon having made 378 appearances for the Anfield club

‘I think when I overtook Darren Fletcher (80 caps), when I was in the 80s, it felt like ages for me to get to Jim Leighton (91). Then I thought I’ve only got one more person to go.

‘That’s when I started thinking about it a little bit more, starting to believe that it might happen, started to wind Kenny up a bit more that it was going to happen.

‘I think that was maybe when I realised that this was maybe possible if I got lucky with injuries, if I kept playing for Liverpool.

‘Sat here today, if it happens, it’s something I couldn’t be more proud of. My international career has been everything for me.’

To wear the armband at one international tournament would have been a laudable achievement in itself. To do so three times would have seemed an impossible feat in those difficult early days.

The hunger to repeat the trick at Euro 2028 is as strong as ever.

‘I’ve always kept pushing,’ he said. ‘We’re always trying something new. My wife asked me a similar question last week when we were talking about it. I was going to try and catch Gemma Fay (203 caps), but I think that might be a little bit too far from me...’

#1804. Arsenal starlet sent off after nightmare performance as England U19s routed

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Marli Salmon was sent off as England Under-19s fell to a heavy defeat against Austria.

The 17-year-old made his debut for that age group last week in a comfortable win over Slovenia, having been called up as an injury replacement.

However, it was a much more difficult game for Salmon on Tuesday as his afternoon came to a premature end.

The Arsenal defender got the nod against Austria and it was an eventful start to the match, with three goals inside the opening ten minutes.

Austria scored again before half-time to lead 3-1 and that was still the scoreline heading into the final 20 minutes of the match.

Salmon was booked for dissent, having shouted in the referee’s face and waved his arm angrily after conceding a free-kick.

Four minutes later, the teenager was then shown a straight red card to complete a miserable occasion for him.

Reigan Heskey played a loose pass back that left his team-mates scrambling and Salmon could not cut out the danger on the halfway line.

Austria’s Johannes Moser got to the ball first and was running clean through on goal, only for Salmon to slide in and bring him down.

He immediately punched the ground in frustration and did not even look back at the referee, knowing the red card was coming, and he began trudging off the pitch.

Austria went on to score another goal with the man advantage and secure a 4-1 win.

It is the second international break in a row that an Arsenal player has been sent off for the England U19s.

Max Dowman was shown a straight red card last month against the USA for a reckless challenge.

Salmon was shown a straight red card for dissent while captaining Arsenal’s Under-21s in a 1-0 defeat by Ipswich Town back in Feburary. He signed his first professional deal with the Gunners in April.
